I think people have a narrow understanding of the idea of "prediction".  They always think of it at the local or immediate level when it comes to LLMs, that LLMs are predicting language solely as the associations were presented to them.  Just parroting what they've seen happen before.

But "prediction" can also happen at the meta level.  This is what humans do - a scientist who forms a hypothesis, an artist that invents a new style, a philosopher realizing a new paradigm before anyone else can see it.  Humans are "prediction models" just as LLMs are, except we routinely form unique associations from our input before we practice our "prediction".  What we've felt is our unique talent is our ability to think about and organize input data in a manner that's efficient for meta prediction.

And that's what this research is showing from Google - that LLMs are learning how to similarly predict at the meta level, forming unique associations of their own.  Perhaps at a very limited scale by comparison, but it's happening.
